body.statement: The explicitly dimensioned law \(P^{\star}\) is a strictly positive Markov law for the graph with measurement matrix \(\Gamma^{\star}\) and empty latent DAG; it satisfies measurement nondegeneracy, double triangularity, third-view coverage, and the subset condition. The third latent coordinate has no pure child, and the displayed selected matrices satisfy \(\det(B_{a,k,u})=(c^{\star}_{s(a,k),\rho_a(k)})^2>0\), so \(\Delta_{\mathrm{DT}}>0\). These support, graph, nondegeneracy, and certificate properties persist on a relatively open neighborhood of \(P^{\star}\). Every such neighborhood contains a rational faithful law on the same graph; each such law belongs to \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cert}}^{(3)}(3,8)\), has an identified recovery target, and supplies a dense ternary no-pure-child witness.
body.justification: The witness demonstrates a positive no-pure-child ternary region and makes every certificate matrix inspectable.
body.gap: Lee and Gu (2026) give binary no-pure-child examples and ternary failures, but no positive certified ternary model supporting the full chain.
body.consumer: It is an exact regression test and simulation fixture for a \(\texttt{cdmTools}\)-style checker.
body.proof_tex:
Write \(C_k=\operatorname{ch}_X(H_k)\) for the observed-child set of the \(k\)-th latent coordinate.  Reading the columns of \(\Gamma^{\star}\) gives
\[
 C_1=\{1,2,3,5,6,7\},\qquad
 C_2=\{2,3,4,5,6,8\},\qquad
 C_3=\{3,6,7,8\}.
\]
For each ordered pair of distinct sets, the differences are nonempty: for example, \(1\in C_1\setminus C_2\), \(4\in C_2\setminus C_1\), \(1\in C_1\setminus C_3\), \(8\in C_3\setminus C_1\), \(2\in C_2\setminus C_3\), and \(7\in C_3\setminus C_2\).  Hence no one of these child sets contains another.

Rows \(1,2,3\) have diagonal parents \(1,2,3\), respectively, in the order \((1,2,3)\), and none has a parent later than its diagonal parent in that order.  Rows \(4,5,6\) have diagonal parents \(2,1,3\), respectively, in the order \((2,1,3)\), with the same zero pattern for later parents.  This proves double triangularity for the displayed \(S_1,S_2,\rho_1,\rho_2\).  In \(S_3=\{7,8\}\), row \(7\) is a child of latent coordinates \(1,3\), while row \(8\) is a child of coordinates \(2,3\); thus every latent coordinate has an \(S_3\)-child.  Every child \(3,6,7,8\) of \(H_3\) has at least two latent parents, so \(H_3\) has no pure child.

For a fixed observed row \(j\), the displayed conditional probabilities are normalized because, for every \(h_\ell\in\{0,1,2\}\),
\[
 \sum_{x=0}^{2}
 \left(\mathbf 1\{x=h_\ell\}-\frac13\right)=0.
\]
Moreover,
\[
 \sum_{\ell:\,\Gamma^{\star}_{j\ell}=1}c^{\star}_{j\ell}
 \le 2^{-(4+j)}\sum_{\ell=1}^{3}8^{-\ell}
 <\frac1{224}.
\]
Since \(-1/3\le \mathbf 1\{x=h_\ell\}-1/3\le2/3\), every measurement-table entry lies in the interval
\[
 \left(\frac13-\frac1{3\cdot224},
       \frac13+\frac2{3\cdot224}\right)\subset(0,1).
\]
Combining these tables by conditional independence across the observed coordinates with the independent uniform latent law gives the Markov factorization for the graph with empty latent DAG.  All latent weights and all measurement-table entries are strictly positive, so the resulting complete-data law \(P^{\star}\) is strictly positive.

To prove measurement nondegeneracy, fix \(j\) and two different configurations \(h,h'\) of its latent parents.  Let \(\ell_0\) be the smallest parent index for which \(h_{\ell_0}\ne h'_{\ell_0}\), and evaluate the difference of the two conditional mass functions at \(x=h_{\ell_0}\).  Terms with index smaller than \(\ell_0\) cancel, the \(\ell_0\)-term equals \(c^{\star}_{j\ell_0}\), and the remaining terms have total absolute value at most
\[
 \sum_{\substack{\ell>\ell_0\\
                   \Gamma^{\star}_{j\ell}=1}}
 c^{\star}_{j\ell}
 <c^{\star}_{j\ell_0}
   \sum_{r=1}^{\infty}8^{-r}
 =\frac17c^{\star}_{j\ell_0}.
\]
The evaluated difference is therefore nonzero.  Thus distinct parent configurations induce distinct conditional distributions.

Because the latent coordinates are independent, conditioning on a predecessor context does not change the distribution of any later latent coordinate.  Separating the diagonal-parent term in each selected measurement table consequently gives
\[
 B_{a,k,u}
 =b^{\star}_{s(a,k),u}\mathbf 1^{\mathsf T}
  +c^{\star}_{s(a,k),\rho_a(k)}Q_3.
\]
Set \(t=c^{\star}_{s(a,k),\rho_a(k)}\) and \(b=b^{\star}_{s(a,k),u}\).  Since \(\mathbf 1^{\mathsf T}b=1\), the decomposition
\[
 \mathbb R^3=\operatorname{span}\{\mathbf 1\}
 \oplus\{v:\mathbf 1^{\mathsf T}v=0\}
\]
shows that \(Bv=tv\) on the two-dimensional zero-sum subspace, while
\[
 B\mathbf 1=3b
 =\mathbf 1+3\left(b-\frac13\mathbf 1\right).
\]
In a basis adapted to this decomposition, \(B\) is block triangular with diagonal entries \(1,t,t\).  Therefore
\[
 \det(B_{a,k,u})=t^2
 =\left(c^{\star}_{s(a,k),\rho_a(k)}\right)^2>0.
\]
Definition~\textnormal{def:certificate} then gives \(\Delta_{mathrm{DT}}>0\).

Strict positivity is a finite collection of strict inequalities.  Measurement nondegeneracy is also witnessed by finitely many strict inequalities between table columns, and the certificate condition is witnessed by finitely many nonzero determinants.  These properties therefore persist in a relatively open neighborhood \(U\) of the displayed table parameter; the graph properties persist because the graph is fixed.  By Lemma~\textnormal{lem:positive-faithful-parameters-dense}, the faithful positive Markov parameters are dense and relatively open, so every nonempty relative open subset of \(U\) meets that set in a nonempty relative open set.  Rational simplex coordinates are dense in the affine product of table simplices.  Hence every such neighborhood contains a rational parameter that is faithful and retains all the preceding strict properties.  Its induced joint law is rational because the Markov factorization uses only finite sums and products of rational table entries.

Every rational law so obtained satisfies all member properties in Definition~\textnormal{def:certified-class}, and hence belongs to \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cert}}^{(3)}(3,8)\).  Theorem~\textnormal{thm:fixed-k-identification} then identifies its quotient recovery target from its observed law.  The already verified child sets and the absence of a pure child of \(H_3\) are unchanged.  This proves every assertion, without requiring the particular displayed parameter \(P^{\star}\) itself to be faithful.
